why: no prior candidate was worth the fixed read budget

Second manifest was dominated by domain surveys and generic LLM-agent surveys, not primary methods on search completeness, contradiction handling, calibration, source overlap, or adaptive stopping; reading them would waste scrutiny and bias toward topical keyword overlap.

PRISMA-S is the primary consensus reporting extension governing reproducible search trace; Ioannidis 2016 is a primary meta-research critique of redundant, misleading and conflicted review production, useful as disconfirming evidence against assuming more synthesis automatically improves epistemic quality.

decision: Decompose methodological evidence into focused retrieval rounds and reject off-target manifests rather than padding reads.
why: The default router classified this meta-research question as products/consumer and the first broad academic retrieval produced irrelevant topical surveys. To avoid keyword-driven noise, the node will use explicit channel overrides and separate exact-method queries for reporting/recall, stopping, dependence/contradiction, and contextual synthesis.

The journal guideline article and the Canadian health-technology agency update report are the primary PRESS outputs; the latter contains the systematic review/survey/consensus provenance behind the checklist. They are same-origin evidence and will not be treated as independent corroboration.

The PMC article is the full primary 1996 methods study applying capture-recapture to estimate missed studies and search completeness; other candidates are secondary copies, a short conference abstract, or unrelated results.

Booth 2010 is the primary methodological review explicitly comparing exhaustive with optimal retrieval and candidate stopping approaches. The NIHR HTA review is an independent systematic synthesis of dissemination/publication biases, testing the assumption that searching only published/indexed sources can be complete.

The BMJ article is the primary audit of where 495 included sources actually came from in a complex review, directly testing database-only search. The Nature correspondence is a distinct-origin methodological counterpoint defending protocol-driven searching, included to preserve the live disagreement rather than convert one audit into a universal rule.

Pieper et al. is the primary empirical paper introducing corrected covered area to quantify repeated primary studies across reviews. The newer wCCA paper is an independent methodological extension that exposes CCA limitations by weighting informational overlap; together they inform origin-level dependence rather than domain-counting.

The BMJ PDF is the primary SWiM reporting guideline, directly addressing how to synthesize heterogeneous evidence transparently when statistical pooling is inappropriate; other top candidates duplicate or summarize the same work.

The 2011 GRADE inconsistency paper and its 2023 update are the primary methodological lineage for judging unexplained disagreement. They are same-origin guidance, read together to avoid presenting superseded criteria as independent corroboration.

This is the primary CERQual guidance paper defining transparent, finding-level confidence judgments across methodological limitations, coherence, adequacy and relevance—directly applicable to non-quantitative field-survey claims.

decision: Stop methods retrieval at local saturation and preserve named gaps instead of continuing for superficial source count.
why: Ten focused rounds covered reproducible search reporting/peer review, adaptive retrieval, measurable stopping/completeness, publication bias, source overlap and informational dependence, contradiction/inconsistency judgment, and qualitative confidence/context. The last rounds added refinements (wCCA, updated GRADE, CERQual) rather than a new methodological family; remaining uncertainty is empirical transfer to agentic research, which requires A/B evaluation rather than more literature retrieval.
